lessons: Tonight contradicted the guide: WG ran 9 Forest/8 Plains with Avacyn's Pilgrim and went 3-0 in matches (6-2 in games), not 0-3 or 1-2 as the guide claims.
Fliers plus removal won: Angel of Flight Alabaster, Midnight Haunting, Gallows Warden, Orchard Spirit, Spidery Grasp, Bonds of Faith, Urgent Exorcism, Slayer of the Wicked; take fliers over filler.
Kruin Outlaw was a stranded pack 2 first pick in my WG deck; once pack 1 sets two colours, take on-colour removal over off-colour rares, as the guide says.
Heretic's Punishment, taken early in pack 3 and left out of my UB deck, was the removal I needed; my games stalled for 18 to 21 turns without enough answers, so take cheap removal over more bodies.
I lost 0-2 to WU's fliers (Stitched Drake, Moon Heron, Invisible Stalker), and my two Vampire Interlopers can't block, so prioritise flying blockers and removal for them.
Fliers did not win against WG: our WU lost 0-2 to Somberwald Spider, Spidery Grasp, Bonds of Faith and Urgent Exorcism, so count reach and flier answers before trusting the guide's fliers-win advice.
WG sideboarded Naturalize after game 1 against our auras, Claustrophobia and Ghostly Possession, so prefer non-aura answers like Grasp of Phantoms when the opponent may have enchantment removal.
Our WU deck ran Armored Skaab and two Stitcher's Apprentice without a self-mill plan, against the guide's skip list; avoid mill-yourself cards outside UG.
Don't spend pack 2's first pick on Victim of Night unless you're heading into black; my UR deck never played it, so that early pick was wasted.
My UR deck lost both 1-2 rounds in 15 to 21 turn games, so prioritize card advantage and removal like Claustrophobia over extra bodies such as the second Riot Devils.
Cutting blue spells to reach 17 lands left my deck thin on answers against grindy WU and UB decks, so keep playable blue spells that trade for value.
Commit by mid pack 1: my Dead Weight, Invisible Stalker, Into the Maw of Hell and Disciple of Griselbrand were stranded, leaving WG with only Spidery Grasp and Urgent Exorcism as removal.
Round 3's 1-2 loss to WG shows removal count matters: my answers to their fliers were thin, so take a third removal spell over a second Grave Bramble.
Count evasion: my WG had only Voiceless Spirit, Orchard Spirit and Somberwald Spider in the air; take a third flier like Chapel Geist over Festerhide Boar.
Red burn was the backbone: Geistflame, Harvest Pyre, and Brimstone Volley did the removal work, so take cheap burn over marginal creatures in packs 1 and 2.

The 0-2 loss to the green-white deck came in 17- and 30-turn grinds, where my ground creatures stalled, so draft real evasion and card advantage earlier rather than stacking evasive-ish vampires and werewolves.

When cutting to 23 spells, I dropped the second Skirsdag Cultist and Curse of the Pierced Heart for Stensia Bloodhall, keeping Bloodgift Demon, Night Revelers, and Rage Thrower as finishers; that build went 2-1.
Mono-white with only three fliers stalled into a 40-turn loss to WG, confirming the guide's 'fliers win' claim, so take a second colour's fliers or removal before a third Village Bell-Ringer.
Mono-white ignored red burn, and BR's Geistflame and Harvest Pyre beat me 0-2, so take Geistflame and Brimstone Volley over filler like Thraben Purebloods.
Pack 2 black picks (Typhoid Rats, Vampiric Fury, Spare from Evil) went unplayed, so commit to your second colour by mid-pack 2 instead of hedging.
Prioritise cheap removal over Markov Patrician: I took Patrician twice, and my UB deck ran only four removal spells. Fiend Hunter, Brimstone Volley and Claustrophobia beat me.
Once black is settled, don't spend mid-pack-2 picks on off-colour removal like Harvest Pyre. It became a dead card while my UB deck lacked interaction.
My losses to BR and UR went 15-22 turns with a stalled board, so prioritise evasive finishers and card advantage such as Bloodgift Demon over a second Markov Patrician.
